avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, controlling emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and has them planted on public land, and pays an organization to green private and institutional sites. Boroughs add their own means: park fund money, equipment rental, blue-collar crews. Variances also govern tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water, maintain and replace some of them. The maximum expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees distributed across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its reserved fund for park purposes toward buying trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an expansion at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar crews assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with renovating the parc Pratt chalet and redeveloping its surroundings, including planting vegetation, partly financed by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council leases land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees intended for planting there.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its report and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood nursery runs until April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.titre: Spring cleaning of streets and sidewalks
etapes.texte: Several boroughs are renting vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to remove abrasives after winter. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing an expense of $574,920.99, taxes included, for four vacuum sweepers and three tanker trucks in 2026 and 2027.

etapes.titre: Snow removal from downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is entrusting companies with maintenance, cleanliness and snow removal for Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises, square Dorchester, place du Canada, îlot Bonaventure, square Victoria, place du Sable-Gris and square Chaboillez. The borough is also extending snow removal for the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027.

Montréal-Nord is paying for an additional rented grader during the 2025-2026 winter, and Saint-Léonard is allocating $200,000 in surplus to its 2026 snow removal operations, after 39 abrasive spreadings since November 15, 2025, while the budget had planned for 20. The City and some boroughs are extending turnkey snow removal, towing and equipment rental with operators contracts by 12 months.

etapes.titre: Snow removal for parks and buildings
etapes.texte: The City is extending snow removal for the parking lot of the édifice Jacinthe-Fyfe and for parc Frédéric-Back, the TAZ and the stade de soccer de Montréal. It is also awarding a contract to remove snow from service roads and parking lots in the Grand parc de l'Ouest, in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal services for the Grand parc de l'Ouest cover two seasons, from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
The extended towing contracts start on November 15, 2026.
The turnkey snow removal contract for Le Plateau-Mont-Royal ends on April 15, 2031, with each season running from November 1 to April 15.
The turnkey snow removal contracts for Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Le Sud-Ouest end on April 15, 2030.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is funding and launching work on its water and sewer pipes, on streets in several boroughs as well as on the main network. It is continuing the replacement of lead service lines, including the portion located on private land. It is also investing in the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, where it is building a wastewater disinfection unit and maintaining existing facilities.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council increases from $197,000,000 to $381,000,000 the loan funding the effluent disinfection unit at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant. The money is used notably to finish the ozonation unit and to build the oxygen production plant that will supply it.

The City awards several contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes without trenching and to redo roadways, on streets in many boroughs. These projects include the replacement of lead water service connections, on both the public and private sides.

The City awards contracts to rebuild water pipes on rue Guy and on rue De Champlain, and adds funds to the projects on rue Saint-Antoine Ouest and rue de la Cathédrale, up to the McTavish reservoir. It is also leasing from Parks Canada a 941-square-metre plot of land under the canal de Lachine to maintain two 600-millimetre pipes.

aSurveiller.texte: Start-up of the ozone plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant expected in 2029; the contracts for lots 4, 5 and 6 are to end in the last quarter of 2028.
Shutdown of sludge incinerator 2 starting the first week of October 2026, and of incinerator 4 in January 2027, for about six weeks of work each.
Adoption of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for secondary networks announced for October 19, 2026.
Rue Guy project planned from the second quarter of 2026 to December 2027.
Work on rue de la Cathédrale, up to the McTavish reservoir, extended until March 2027.
Inspection of main pipes by Pure Technologies: starting in July 2026, ending in June 2028.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned landfill, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward on several fronts at parc Frédéric-Back and the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel: a greenhouse complex in the southwest sector of the park, electrical work related to biogas capture, and routine maintenance of the park. It is also requesting financial assistance from the Québec government for an east-west pedestrian and cycling link, and for rue De Louvain Est alongside the park.

etapes.titre: Funding request for the east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for assistance of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre multi-use path crossing the park, with a footbridge of about 150 metres. The project also includes stormwater management works and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

etapes.titre: Green light for the greenhouse project
etapes.texte: The conseil d'agglomération approves the construction of a greenhouse complex near the composting platform: 1,500 m² for research and training, 1,000 m² for the Saint-Michel neighbourhood's community greenhouse, with a construction budget estimated at $2,185,000. The agglomeration entrusts the project to the conseil municipal, which accepts the offer from the arrondissement of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension to lead the construction site.

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. a contract of $1,091,693.37, taxes included, for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel. The work includes a new 25 kV power supply, a transformer, a backup generator and a central controller to manage biogas capture.

The City entrusts general maintenance of the park to Groupe Nicky and ecological and horticultural management to Entreprises Roseneige, for 30 months starting May 1, 2026. It is also extending the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor, with the compost used for park landscaping, and extending park, TAZ and soccer stadium snow removal services by six months.

The borough is awarding Les industries Harnois inc. the supply and installation of two greenhouses at the park, for a maximum amount of $499,865.92, taxes included, and is authorizing a total expenditure of $574,845.80 including contingencies. Only one company bid out of the five that obtained the bid documents.

The borough is awarding Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue De Louvain between the park and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 taxes included, with a total authorized expenditure of $11,192,464.62: sewers, water mains, lighting, walking corridors, cycling facilities and plantings. In October, it authorizes the filing of a financial assistance request to the ministère des Transports for a bike lane and sidewalks on this same section.

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the TAPU program, for which the City is requesting financial assistance, closes on November 26, 2026.
For the greenhouses, infrastructure delivery is scheduled for July 2026, construction start in August 2026 and completion in December 2026; commissioning is announced for winter 2027.
The snow removal extension covers November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
The rue De Louvain construction site takes place in three phases: May to November 2026, May to October 2027 and May to August 2028.
The park maintenance contracts run until October 31, 2028, with two possible 12-month extensions; 26 hectares will be added in 2027 in the Boisé Ouest sector.

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, in the process of being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.titre: More money for the heritage walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77, taxes included. The file explains the costs by unforeseen site conditions: buried stones that had to be cleaned by hand, extra mortar, sod, and a deteriorated culvert that needs replacing.

The City is submitting an application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques area (330 hectares) for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. The application does not commit any spending; if the designation is granted, the City commits to producing a lighting plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping the site accessible at night.

etapes.titre: Two areas listed as natural areas
etapes.texte: The parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme area of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) are added to the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité de l'agglomération (registry of natural areas protected and contributing to biodiversity in the urban agglomeration), along with conservation plans. The 2025 report filed shows 4,051 ha listed or provisionally listed, representing 8.1% of the urban agglomeration's territory.

A contract worth $366,117.31, taxes included, is awarded to Gendron Gestion Civil inc. to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub; total spending reaches $481,850.45, taxes included. The undersized culvert had been damaged by the heavy rains of August 2024.

etapes.titre: Snow removal, cleaning and tree felling
etapes.texte: The City is awarding Paysagiste Solarco inc. the contract for snow removal on service roads and parking lots in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche, and Cap-Saint-Jacques areas ($178,330.82, taxes included), and 9232-3914 Québec inc. the cleaning of nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings ($704,619.24, taxes included). Entrepreneur Paysagiste Strathmore (1997) ltée will fell ash trees and other declining trees in the park, for a total expenditure of $1,713,041.27, taxes included.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal on service roads and parking lots from November 1, 2026, to April 30, 2028.
Cleaning of nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings from November 1, 2026, to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension to October 31, 2031.
Felling of ash trees and declining trees from fall 2026 to early summer 2028.
Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan to be filed in February 2027, DarkSky International's response expected in April 2027, full compliance of the site by April 2032.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warm-up spots, and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations so they can open warm-up spots, and it funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It is also deploying a Ville-Marie public works team to other boroughs for cleanliness interventions related to homelessness. It is setting up a framework for receiving private donations and is appealing a ruling on encampments under the viaduc Van Horne.

etapes.texte: The City lends three buildings free of charge to organizations for the winter: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former monastery of the Recluses Missionnaires at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. The loans end on April 30, 2026, and the value of the unbilled rent is estimated at $57,076 for the church.

Verdun pays $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville ratifies the continuation of the contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. for a warm-up spot for the winter of 2025-2026.

The City grants financial support to community organizations under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028, for inclusion, public space cohabitation, and awareness projects. The amounts cover a three-year period ending December 31, 2028.

etapes.titre: Private donations and the Bain St-Denis layout
etapes.texte: City council adopts a framework for receiving private donations for housing, shelter, and social cohabitation projects; donors do not choose which project is funded. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for the activities and layout work of the temporary warm-up spot at the Bain Saint-Denis. City council also adopts a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness and a motion on a rent support fund.

etapes.titre: Encampments on rue Notre-Dame and appeal of the ruling
etapes.texte: The City awards a $149,520 contract, taxes included, to Mission Old Brewery to help people from the rue Notre-Dame encampment area move toward shelter and housing, and pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027, and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. The executive committee takes charge of the dispute over the encampments under the viaduc Van Horne and authorizes an appeal of the June 8, 2026 ruling.

aSurveiller.texte: Mission Old Brewery's mandate in the rue Notre-Dame encampment area ends on October 18, 2026.
The agreement between Ville-Marie and Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for the public works team runs until May 15, 2027.
Support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanization and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is changing the days, sectors and frequency of collections in several boroughs, and buying bins for residents. It is extending its food waste treatment contracts and its contracts related to ecocentres, and awarding a contract to recover mattresses. It is also tabling the agglomeration's 2025 residual materials management report.

etapes.texte: The City is extending its contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. twice, by six months each time, to compost or biomethanize food waste from the east of the agglomeration. The materials are transferred in Montréal-Est and then treated in Saint-Thomas-de-Joliette and Moose Creek, Ontario, while awaiting the start-up of the Montréal-Est organic materials treatment centre.

etapes.titre: Bin purchase and lending of sorting equipment
etapes.texte: City council enters into agreements with Orbis Canada and USD Global to supply collection bins to residents of the boroughs, then with Plasti-Bac inc. for garbage bins for Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. The executive committee approves an agreement with Tricentris, which pays $43,773.61, taxes included, for a program to lend reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations at neighbourhood events.

etapes.titre: Containers, ecocentres and former dump sites
etapes.texte: The agglomeration is extending the contracts for garbage collection from front-loading and semi-underground containers, as well as the container contract for the Saint-Laurent ecocentre. It is awarding Recyc-Matelas inc. a contract worth $734,690.25, taxes included, to collect and recover mattresses and box springs from ecocentres, assigning two firms to carry out studies on buildings located on former waste disposal sites, and extending the contract for the software that manages dumping authorizations.

aSurveiller.texte: The dishware, water fountain and sorting station lending program is offered until December 31, 2026 at the latest.
The extension of the food waste treatment contracts runs until February 28, 2027.
The Saint-Laurent ecocentre container contract and the container collection contracts are extended until October 31, 2027.
The dumping authorization management software contract covers the period from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new district on the site of the former Blue Bonnets hippodrome: sale of land, loan by-laws, waterworks for the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: The City is preparing the future district on the site of the former Blue Bonnets hippodrome, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It got an extension from Québec to sell a first parcel of land, adopted two loan by-laws for waterworks and public domain works, and transferred a parcel of land to an organization for non-market housing. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: Deadline postponed to sell a first parcel of land
etapes.texte: The Government of Québec grants the City a deadline until October 31, 2027 to sell a first parcel of land on the site of the former hippodrome, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The postponement does not involve any financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer deed remain the same.

City council approves a $2,000,000 City guarantee in favour of the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to Société GALOPH used to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. On the same day, council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and the management of assets and public funds in the development of the district.

The City borrows $29,000,000 to develop the district's public domain: soil remediation, sewers and waterworks, street redevelopment, fees and land purchases. It also borrows $12,000,000 to build main water mains between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

etapes.titre: Four buildings authorized on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four residential buildings in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur. One of the buildings must house a municipal sports and recreation centre, and the developer must pay $3,200,000 for public amenities and facilities in the sector.

The City leases parcels of the site to the community cafeteria MultiCaf and to the Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora for temporary urban agriculture, as well as to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a transition nursery. Each lease provides for a token rent, and the organizations pay for development, maintenance and property taxes.

aSurveiller.texte: Deadline granted by the Government of Québec to sell a first parcel of the site: October 31, 2027.
The $128.3M federal grant is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by 2031; the funds from the $29,000,000 loan cover work from 2026 to 2028.
Communia has five years after the signing of the transfer deed to complete at least one building, and housing affordability must last at least 25 years.
End of temporary leases: April 30, 2027 for MultiCaf, March 31, 2028 for Polliflora, and April 30, 2028 for the transition nursery.

parcs.description: Development and repair of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: The City is designing and redoing parks in several boroughs: soil studies, work contracts, public art, and adjustments to projects already underway. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, it is having walls and a culvert repaired, submitting an application for a designation related to the night sky, and awarding snow removal, housekeeping, and tree felling contracts to companies. Several projects are funded by the participatory budget, the environmental liability reserve, or park funds.

etapes.titre: Design, soil studies and financing agreement
etapes.texte: The City awards the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of the parc Le Prévost to a competition-winning team, for a total expense of $10,559,257.81 including taxes. It also pays $174,471.56 to Verdun for studies before redoing the parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, and the Sud-Ouest signs an agreement with Hydro-Québec to obtain $154,000 for the parc d'Argenson.

etapes.titre: Grand parc de l'Ouest: work and protection
etapes.texte: The City adds $162,897.98 to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville and awards a contract to rebuild the culvert under that same road, in the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub. It submits the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for the Urban Night Sky Place designation and registers the Anse-à-l'Orme sector, along with the parc-nature des Sources, in the directory of protected natural environments.

The City adds $153,434.14 to the supervision of work at the parc du Bassin-à-Bois and $168,472.14 to decontaminate the parc George-Vernot. The boroughs move or increase budgets for the parcs des Hirondelles, du Sault-au-Récollet, Villeray, and Percy-Walters.

etapes.titre: Maintenance of the Grand parc de l'Ouest
etapes.texte: The agglomeration awards contracts for snow removal of service roads and parking lots in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche, and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors, housekeeping of nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings, and the felling of ash trees and dying trees.

aSurveiller.texte: Selection of the winning public art project for the parc des Eaux-Cachées in October 2026, contract with the artist in December 2026, and installation of the artwork in 2028.
Adoption expected at city council on October 19, 2026 to transfer a 75.2 m² strip of laneway to the parc Le Prévost.
Start of the snow removal and housekeeping contracts for the Grand parc de l'Ouest on November 1, 2026.
Response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027 for Cap-Saint-Jacques, with the lighting plan to be submitted in February 2027.
Final acceptance of the work at the parc du Bassin-à-Bois expected in June 2027.
Completion of the work at the parc J.O.R.-Leduc expected in June 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and business-animation by-laws.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is funding and regulating temporary pedestrian streets on commercial thoroughfares, mainly for the 2026 summer season. The executive committee paid $2,694,500 to the boroughs under the call for projects for pedestrianization on commercial thoroughfares [CE26 0465], and the boroughs adopted the by-laws that close the streets and allow terraces, sales and music. Other decisions concern public squares: landscaping, a change in a lot's status, and an official name.

etapes.titre: Grant rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law allowing it to subsidize its business development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre, provided that council closes the street by by-law [CA26 240037]. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer [CA26 26 0010].

The executive committee allocates $2,694,500 among boroughs for pedestrian streets closed for at least eight consecutive weeks, including rue Villeray as a new project [CE26 0465]. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce creates the Placette CDN from April 1 to October 31, 2026 [CA26 170058], and Ville-Marie prohibits traffic on the sections of its summer pedestrianizations [CA26 240090].

The boroughs pay contributions to the business development corporations that organize the pedestrian streets: $102,045 for rue Villeray [CA26 14 0078], $375,500 for rue Sainte-Catherine Est [CA26 240134] and $67,500 for avenue Lacombe until 2028 [CA26 170108]. Outremont allocates $105,000 to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique [CA26 16 0061].

Borough councils close their thoroughfares to cars and regulate terraces, sales and noise: avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24 [CA26 16 0082], avenues Royal and Madison from June 1 to October 31 [CA26 170088], rue Ontario Est from June 15 to September 18 [CA26 27 0115], avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth [CA26 25 0134]. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations [CA26 240155] and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve removes 113 paid parking spaces [CA26 27 0119].

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council changes the status of a 899-square-metre lot at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier from a street (public square) to a local park [CM26 0888] and names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque "place Chez-Marguerite" [CM26 0913]. Ville-Marie authorizes sound ambiance on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles [CA26 240372] and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal revises the reopening schedule for avenue du Mont-Royal [CA26 25 227].

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, and between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
The boroughs must report on the amounts received for pedestrianizations in November 2026 and return unspent money in December 2026.
The by-law on the sound ambiance of the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transit contract on avenue du Mont-Royal covers up to December 31, 2027, and support for the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe up to December 31, 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws that each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie reviews its rules on urban planning, special projects and demolition, and Saint-Léonard amends its by-law on special projects and its by-law on building demolition.

The borough changes the heights, uses and site coverage ratio in the sector bounded by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increases the allowed heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevard Crémazie and boulevard Henri-Bourassa.

After a public consultation on March 18, 2026 and a written consultation from March 11 to 18, 2026, the borough amends its zoning (list of heritage buildings of interest), its regulations on demolition, conditional uses, special projects and site planning and architectural integration plans. The new rules notably govern housing for people experiencing residential instability and the studies required before any work on a heritage building.

The borough tables a first draft in March, holds a public consultation on March 25, 2026, then adopts in May a by-law covering urban planning, special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. The text authorizes a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and requires approval for building an in-ground pool within the declared heritage site of Mont-Royal.

etapes.titre: Two requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève requests six additional months, citing staff shortages, the complexity of its territory and coordination with the Service de l'urbanisme.

aSurveiller.texte: The Minister of Municipal Affairs set June 16, 2027 as the deadline for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; the replacement of its zoning by-law is part of the blocks that follow.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws, and its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting an extension until June 16, 2027 to adopt its concordance by-laws.

securite-publique.description: The City of Montréal's Police Department (SPVM): contracts, neighbourhood police stations, council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of a police officer
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to buy and replace specialized SPVM equipment between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a sergeant-detective to the RCMP team that enforces the Firearms Act, for three years starting January 7, 2026.

The City buys 11 patrol motorcycles, extends the housekeeping contract for headquarters by one year, and awards work to replace the oil heating at the cavalry building, at 1515 chemin Remembrance. It also awards a meal contract for detained persons and extends maintenance of the call dispatch system software.

The City leases 50 parking spaces at 260 boulevard De Maisonneuve for headquarters vehicles. It renews the leases for the training centre in Anjou, neighbourhood police station 15 in Verdun, and neighbourhood police station 26 on avenue Mountain Sights.

The City enters into an agreement to supply 9 mm practice ammunition used for police firearms training, and extends the SPVM's mail pickup and distribution service by one year. It also retains suppliers for carpentry and painting services in the department's buildings.

aSurveiller.texte: "Fèves au lard" fundraising day at neighbourhood police station 46, on October 23, 2026; the borough of Anjou buys 62 tickets.
The port patrol boat and its trailer must be delivered no later than March 1, 2027.
The lease for the metro unit premises of neighbourhood police station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, starts on February 1, 2027.
The ACCES Tabac, Alcool, Cannabis and ACCEF committees are extended until March 31, 2027.
The work to replace the oil heating at the cavalry building must be completed by September 30, 2027.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.

velo.titre: Cycling: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the self-service bike system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City mainly bought equipment for the BIXI self-service bike system, paid for work on existing bike lanes, and settled the occupation of Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs awarded maintenance and development contracts, and the City asked Québec for money for four new cycling projects.

etapes.texte: Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie passed an ordinance that officially establishes the bike lanes on avenue Christophe-Colomb between rues des Carrières and de Bellechasse and imposes mandatory maneuvers on motorists up to Jean-Talon Est. Outremont authorized $100,000 for de-icing salt and abrasives to be spread, notably on its bike paths.

etapes.titre: Bike path repairs and sustainable mobility corridors
etapes.texte: City council added $3,400,000 to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for sustainable mobility corridors in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, then approved Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension carrying out roadway and bike lane work, including repairs to the REV Lajeunesse between Jarry and Crémazie. Ahuntsic-Cartierville hired Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. for spring cleaning of narrow bike paths.

City council awarded a sole-source contract worth $4,815,802.61 to PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. for bikes, stations and docking points compatible with the BIXI system. The executive committee then hired Laser AMP, a division of ISE Métal inc., for $394,851.17, to supply the steel pavers that serve as the base for stations.

Outremont tabled a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal awarded Cojalac inc. work on rue Parthenais including a BIXI station, and the Sud-Ouest awarded Groupe Damex inc. the development of three green alleys and the electrical installation of a BIXI station.

etapes.titre: Requests for financial assistance from Québec
etapes.texte: City council authorized the filing of four financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, for bike lanes and sidewalks on rues de Champlain, Saint-Jacques, Guy and Laurier. The City commits to paying at least half of the eligible expenses.

aSurveiller.texte: October 9, 2026: deadline to submit complete financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.
The repair of the bike lane on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is budgeted at $570,000 in 2027.
